description.text:
a gorgeous, dark-haired woman wearing jaguar fur.
*

items.text: "The strange warrior $P! Surely he has come to rescue Aiela from her cruel prison!"
She looks about fearfully. "Aiela cannot speak to $P now, or Darden's men may hear her and come!"
"Yes, my love?"
Her face darkens. "Oh. It is $P. $P the mate of Tristia. Tristia's mate $P. What does @Tristia's mate $P want?"
"Yes, mighty $P?"
"Aiela is my name. Aiela is daughter of @Aloron, the chief of the @Kuraks."
"Yes?"
"Aiela is Princess of the @Kurak tribe, and warrior. Aiela is friend to the jaguar, enemy of the @Myrmidex."
"Aiela's father is Aloron, chief of the @Kurak tribe."
"Yes?"
"Aiela loves $P, too. Aiela never tires of hearing $P say this."
Her eyes widen. "Is $P saying that he loves Aiela?"
"Aiela belongs to the Kurak tribe. Her father @Aloron is chief of the Kuraks. Kuraks know the jungle and the jungle cats."
"$P is Aiela's mate, and so $P is also a member of the Kurak tribe." She smiles. "Perhaps someday $P will be chief of Kuraks."
"If $P wants bones, he should go to where the great lizards go to die."
"East of the stone city of the @Nahuatla is a great stand of iron bamboo, and north of that is the place where the great lizards go to die."
"Many bones are there."
"When $P has been @Tristia's mate for a while longer, doubtless he will also feel like lying down among those bones and dying there."
"If $P wants a hide, he must kill a furred creature and then use a knife on its carcass. Lizard hide is too tough to be any use."
"A good thing for $P to do with a hide is to make a hide bag and cover the face of his mate @Tristia with it."
"If $P wants iron bamboo, it is easy to find. He must go north of the @Nahuatla stone village, or south of the @Yolaru village, and near the eastern cliffs he will find a great stand of bamboo."
"The Myrmidex! They are evil. Ants of the jungle, but larger than men. No single tribe can stand against them. And yet the tribes will not @unite against them."
"$P has chosen @Tristia as his mate. He must have much in common with the Myrmidex. Perhaps he should go join them."
"Sahree is a warrior-woman of the @Yolaru. Sahree and Aiela are friends and allies."
She adds, playfully: "Sahree is very beautiful, but $P must keep his eyes to Aiela, not Sahree."
"Aiela has heard the name of Topuru. Topuru is a mad shaman, once of the @Urali. Topuru lives on an island, all alone, in the north somewhere."
"The Urali are a suspicious tribe. They hide away from the other tribes. Few ever tell their true names."
"Now that @Darden is dead, their chief is Wamap, who is also their shaman."
"@Darden is still chief among the Urali, though $P has rescued Aiela from him."

"Darden thought he could buy Aiela's love with a giant gem, stolen from the @Nahuatla. But Aiela could never love one so cruel as Darden." She pauses, and grins. "But Aiela did keep the gem. It is very pretty!"
"The Yolaru are a strong, noble tribe east of the @Kuraks. Their chief is Apaton; their shaman is Mosagann; Mosagann has a daughter, @Sahree, who is Aiela's friend."
"The Nahuatla build their village of stone."
"Moctapotl is their chief."
"Huitlapacti is their chief now. Moctapotl was once their chief, but he hides in the jungle, an exile."
"The Disquiqui live west of the @Nahuatla. They do not do much work. They harvest fruits and ferment them into strong drink, and then consume it all."
"Their chief is named Chafblum. He has a daughter named Guoblum."
"You aren't kidding, doll! And keep Guoblum away from me!"
"$P knows well who Tristia is! Tristia has spread word far and wide that she is $P's mate. She crows it to the wind and stars. Why would $P choose someone like Tristia?" She seems almost in tears.
"Tristia? She is Aiela's sister. Not truly: Tristia's father and mother died when their hut burned, so Aiela's father @Aloron raised her."
"But Tristia is cold as the snake. She shows no gratitude to Aloron. And she is greedy. Whatever Aiela has, Tristia must take away."
"There are many tribes in this valley. Aiela will tell $P of them."

"There are the @Kurak, Aiela's tribe, jungle-dwellers. Near the Kurak are the dark-skinned @Yolaru, the @Nahuatla, who build their village of stone, and the @Disquiqui, who make merry all their lives."

"There are many other, more distant tribes: The Pindiro and the Barako, the Jukari and the misshapen Haakur, the Barrab and the lizard-like Sakkhra, the ant-like @Myrmidex, and the @Urali, who had stolen Aiela away."
She kisses you. "But there is only one who may steal Aiela away, and that is $P."
"Aiela has often wished that the tribes would unite against the @Myrmidex. Aiela and her friend @Sahree have discussed this much."
"But the chiefs do not listen to their daughters in such matters." Then her eyes narrow as she looks at you.
"$P has already won Aiela's heart. Aiela is sure that $P could win friendship from the chiefs. Aiela's father @Aloron will already help you."
"Aiela thinks that $P could command respect of the chiefs and @unite all the tribes... if only he would try."
"Aiela thinks that $P could command respect of the chiefs and @unite all the tribes... if only he would try."
"Aiela is already $P's war-companion."
"$P can ask Aiela to @join him if he wishes."
"Aiela will not be ordered! Aiela will stay here if she pleases."
She looks at the surrounding water. "Aiela will not jump into the water."
"Aiela will not wait here for you. Aiela is not $P's @companion, in war or in anything."
She laughs at you. "Wait on the water? $P is funny."
"Aiela is already companion to $P. $P is sometimes forgetful." She grins.
She snorts and turns away.
She delicately traces her hand across your jaw. "Aiela loves talking to $P."
"Aiela will always talk to $P."
She sighs. "Aiela knows nothing of this."
"But she is willing for $P to tell her of it," she adds hopefully.
She glares at you. "But $P has said that he loves @Tristia. $P is cruel and fickle. A worthy mate for Aiela? Ha! He is better suited to the apes of the forest."
Her expression softens from 'furious' to merely 'hurt.' "But perhaps it is true. Does $P truly care for Aiela more than Tristia?"
The hurt look disappears and is gradually replaced by a smile. "Aiela is glad. Aiela has long loved $P, since first she saw him. But when she heard that he preferred @Tristia..."
She steps up and embraces you. "Be true of heart with Aeila, and Aiela will stay true of heart with $P." And she kisses you, her lips sweet as the perfume of a jungle flower.
Her expression turns to one of fury. "$P plays with Aiela's heart! $P is cruel and evil. Leave Aiela alone!"
She throws herself into your arms. "Long has Aiela waited to hear $P say this! Aiela has loved $P since first she saw him."
And she kisses you, passionately losing herself in your embrace for one long moment.
Then she gives you an exasperated look. "$P must not wait so long next time before saying what he feels."
"Oh." She shrinks back a little, then becomes grim-faced and straightens up. "So it is. Aiela is just another warrior to $P."
"$P is just another warrior to Aiela, too." Her jaw trembles just a little, and she turns away from you.
"Join $P? $P who loves she-cat @Tristia? Never!" She turns her back on you.
Her eyes widen. "$P is both bold and cruel! $P has already sent Aiela away from him in disgrace. $P does not @love Aiela. Why should Aiela join $P now?"
"Aiela would love to join $P... when there are fewer people traveling with him."
"Aiela cannot join with $P now! Maybe later."
"Aiela would be proud to be war-companion of the mighty $P."
Her jaw trembles a little. "$P has said he loves Aiela. Now he tells her to leave him. Aiela does not understand."
She looks a little sad. "If $P wishes," she says heavily, "Aiela will leave his company. Aiela enjoyed being his companion." She starts to say something more, but decides against it.
"Does $P mean that he no longer loves Aiela?"
The light goes out of her eyes. "So. $P is cold and cruel as the lizard." She bursts into tears. "He is no fit mate for Aiela."
She breathes a sigh of relief, and smiles. "Aiela would wait for $P forever."
She adds, softly: "And, most important, Aiela's mate."

description.text:
a ruggedly handsome warrior.
*

items.text: "Yes, $P?"
"It is Dokray." (He pronounces it dough-CRAY.)
You see a glimmer of recognition in his eyes. "You speak of a name which is somehow familiar."
"Yes, name is Dokray."
"Dokray quests across all the Valley of @Eodon, fighting bad things like the @Myrmidex."
"Dokray's home is with the @Pindiro, but Dokray visits many other tribes."
He waves his hands as if to encompass all the world. "This land is all the Valley of Eodon. Dokray thought that Eodon was all the world until $P came from outside. So @Intanya says."
He snarls as he speaks. "Myrmidex are ant-like but are the height of men. They are fierce warriors."
"It is not because they have any skill; they do not. But they are without fear and without pain."
"They come into the human villages and kill the people, especially the weak and the young. Dokray hates the Myrmidex. But Dokray cannot make the tribes @unite against them."

"The tribes fight one another, even as the Myrmidex move among them and kill them. The tribes MUST unite to fight the Myrmidex. But Dokray cannot persuade them to unite. The @chiefs will not listen to Dokray."
"Dokray belongs to Pindiro tribe of the north. But..." He frowns. "Dokray was not born a Pindiro."
"Dokray wandered out of the mountains many moons ago, with no memory of his past. The Pindiro adopted Dokray."
"The tribes cannot unite until the chiefs so decree. But when Dokray talks to the chiefs about it, they do not listen. Dokray is a great warrior... but cannot convince with words." He shrugs.
"A man has a name like that. Raf-Kin lives among the @Yolaru."
"The Yolaru are a good tribe. They live east of the Kurak village."
"Dokray knows of a man named Topuru. Topuru is mad. Topuru lives on a little island somewhere in the north, not far from Barako village."
"There are two tribes in the far north: The Pindiro of the plains, Dokray's tribe; and the Barako of the mountains."
"Intanya is shaman of the Kurak tribe. But Intanya is far more."
"Intanya keeps his ear to the ground for all the valley, tries to keep wars between the tribes from becoming too fierce, tries to keep the @Myrmidex at bay."
"Triolo is helper-shaman of Intanya. Triolo sings to himself all the time."
He gives a sly look over to Triolo. "Badly," he adds.
"Triolo heard that!"
Dokray grins.
"Dokray knows of three shamans. Did $P mean the Pindiro shaman @Kunawo, @Intanya or @Triolo?"
"Shamuru is a warrior of the Barako tribe. Very quiet. Good tracker, good hunter. Dokray is better warrior."
He shakes his head. "Dokray did not hear $P very well. Did $P say 'Shaman'?"
"Yes, let us stop talking. Dokray and $P should go find something to smash!"
"If $P wants Dokray to leave, $P has only to ask."
He looks dubiously down at the water. "There are biting fish there. Dokray will wait."
"As $P wishes." Stoically, he waves farewell and goes trudging off.
"No, Dokray has things to do. Dokray will not wait here."
He looks at the water. "There are biting fish here. Dokray would not make it to shore alive. $P is joking, of course."
He nods. "$P must come back for Dokray when $P again needs Dokray's prowess." He waves goodbye.
He gives you a strange look. "Is this a foreign thing? Dokray is already with $P."
"Ask Triolo about that."
"$P must ask another about that."
"Ah. Did $P mean @Intanya or @Triolo?"
"Ah. Then did $P say 'Shamuru'?"
"Shamuru is a warrior of the Barako tribe. Very quiet. Good tracker, good hunter. Dokray is better warrior."
He throws up his hands in puzzlement. "Then Dokray does not understand what $P said. Ask Triolo about that."
He shakes his head, glaring at Ugyuk. "Dokray will not join $P while Ugyuk travels with him."
"Dokray cannot join with $P. $P has too many people with him already."
"Dokray will join with $P when $P is on firm ground."
He considers it briefly, then nods. "Dokray would like hunting with $P. Dokray will join."

description.text:
a lanky, sharp-eyed man in his mid-20s.
*

items.text: "Hey there, $P... about time you got around to showing up!"
"Hey! $P! Go around inside and unlock this door, and let me out of here!"
"Hey, it's your nickel. Talk to me."
"You know, if you've given up on @Aiela, I'd sure like to go after her, myself."
"Too much action muddle your brains, Mr. Adventurer? Jimmy Malone." He scribbles something in his @notebook.
He snaps his fingers impatiently. "That's my name, alright.  Don't wear it out."
"I'm a reporter, see. For the local paper, and I also do pieces for ULTIMATE ADVENTURES @Magazine."
"One of my first will be a 'Modern Man Among the Natives' piece about the @Disquiqui."
"Yeah, it's a nice camera, isn't it? Got a great deal, and it even came with a flash."
He spends a short time showing you how to use it.
"Chafblum. King of the @Disquiqui tribe. One grumpy, evil-tempered son of a gun. Has a face like a washboard somebody's taken a hammer to."
"Oh, those Disquiqui natives. Feed you fermented coconut milk all the time." He shudders. "@Chafblum's the chief. @Guoblum's his daughter."
"She's the Disquiqui princess. Chafblum's daughter. Looks like a statue of Buddha. They want to marry me to her." He shivers.
"Myrmidex. Ant-creatures, big ones. The Disquiqui are scared to death of 'em. They're bad news."
"Yeah, Darden... that big guy with the huge lizard. He's the one who snagged @Aiela when we first got here."
"Glad we managed to get her back with us again!"
"Good thing we managed to get her back to her dad."
"We really should try and find her again, ace."
"What a good-lookin' babe.  Can't blame @Darden for making a move on her."
"ULTIMATE ADVENTURES Magazine. A true-adventure rag I do occasional articles for. I'll have to do a piece on this place. And on you, too. You'll have to tell me your life story sometime."
"Yeah, thrilling to talk to you, too."
"Leave? Hey, I was here first... YOU leave!"
Jimmy looks around and grimaces. "Let's discuss this on dry land."
"Uhhh... if I just leave you, I'm sure that Chafblum's warriors will capture me. Can't I just @wait here?"
"What does it look like I'm doing already? Sheesh."
"I'd much rather wait on dry land... maybe later, $P-old-pal."
"Sure thing, $P-old-pal. It'll give me a chance to catch up on my writing." He whips out his notebook and begins scribbling furiously.
"Hey, I'm already with you."
"My notebook? Nothing in it but some notes on this place. I'm going to write up a doozy of an article for ULTIMATE ADVENTURES Magazine when... IF... we get back."
Jimmy whips out his notebook and flips it to the correct page.
"Oky-doky. Ever since you started talking about uniting the tribes and talking to their chiefs, I've been taking notes. Here's what I've got..."
"Hmmm... sounds like you've heard some interesting stuff out there. Fill me in!"
Jimmy scribbles furiously in his notebook as you spend several minutes telling him what you've learned about uniting the tribes.
"Thanks, boss... this'll make great reading back home! Let me run this back to you, to make sure I've got it."
"Hey, I'd be THRILLED to join you. Get me out of this place and ask me again."
"Sorry, $P... you've got too many people wandering around with you already.  Maybe later."
"Sorry, pal... not when you're on that rickety thing."
"Sure thing, $P-old-pal. To hear is to obey."
"Are we gonna go find that good lookin' babe Aiela now? I thought I heard one of these Disquiqui guys say something about @Darden having captured her."
"Thanks a lot. I'll be right here."
"Okay," he says dejectedly. "If you want me, you know where to find me. At Guoblum's wedding service." He looks like he's been hit by a truck.
"We've already gotten Tuomaxx to rebuild the Great Drum the legends talk about, so that's out of the way."
"We have to build the natives' Great Drum of Legend. We've talked to that butterball Tuomaxx about doing it, but we haven't gotten him all the raw materials he needs to build it."
"We need to build a drum. In lieu of TV, the natives need for some special drum to be built. When all the chiefs' quests are accomplished, we're supposed to beat on it to tell 'em what's up."
"You've already rescued Aiela, what a dish, from Darden the Huge. So her poppa Aloron of the Kurak tribe is in your pocket."
"Aloron of the Kuraks wants you to rescue his daughter Aiela from Darden the Huge. And don't pretend that you don't have some more PERSONAL motivation for that mission, $P-old-pal."
"You haven't yet talked to Aloron, chief of the Kuraks, about what he wants."
"You've already come up with a squad's worth of swords for the Yolaru, so their chief Apaton is 'in.'"
"Apaton, who's the chief of the Yolaru, says that he's tired of the dinosaurs chewing on his people, so he wants ten Nahuatla-made swords for his warriors. Should be a cinch."
"You need to talk to the Yolaru chief Apaton."
"You've already gotten the medicine to fix up Nakai, who's the son of Balakai, chief of the Barrabs. So you're in like Flynn with the Barrabs."
"Nakai, who's the son of Balakai, the Barrab chief, is one sick puppy. Needs some medicine real bad, as I recall, the root of a rare flower on top of the Great Mesa."
"Doesn't sound too dangerous. But Balakai won't give you the time of day until Nakai is healed."
"Balakai's the chief of the Barrab; you haven't talked to him about what he wants."

"We've already belled the cat -- er, the T-Rex, for the Disquiqui. So their chief Chafblum is now your dear friend. And I'm STILL single." He draws a hand across his brow, wiping away imaginary nervous sweat.
"Chafblum, who's the drunkard chief of the Disquiquis, wants me to marry his daughter Guoblum, which ISN'T going to happen!"
"But he'll be your friend if you just hang a bell around the neck of the T-rex which tends to gobble up his tribesmen."
"You don't know what Chafblum wants; he's the chief of the Disquiqui. If he wants me to marry his daughter Guoblum, then this mission is doomed already."
"You've already cleaned out the spider's nest in Haakur territory, so Grugorr, a distant relative at best of Homo Sapiens, is your staunch ally. Hey, I like that phrase. 'Staunch Ally.' Hmmmm..."
"Grugorr, who's the chief of the Haakur -- I think that's a local word for 'missing link' -- wants you to clean out a nest of spiders."
"You also have to burn out their webs, and bring back some leather shield in the spiders' cave."
"Grugorr's the name of the Haakur chief. We don't yet know what he'd want."
"You rescued Halisa, the princess of the Barako, so her mother Halawa's in on whatever expedition you want to lead."

"Halawa, who's the queen of the Barako -- must remind myself to do an 'equal rights in the valley of Eodon' sidebar  -- wants you to rescue her daughter from the big gorilla who's got her. That's one we should do for free."
"I think that the Barako queen is named Halawa. We don't yet know what she'd want to hook up with your mission."
"Ever since we told queen Inara of the Pindiro tribe about your plan to unite the tribes, she's been in our camp."
"@this @should @STILL @never @be @seen"
"We don't yet know what the Pindiro queen Inara wants."
"We managed to cross the lava flow in Jukari territory, and return the sacred hide to their chief, so Jumu is our friend for life."
"Speaking of which, I'll have to get some of those diamonds to take back to the real world... and I'll be SET for life."
"Jumu, the chief of the Jukari, wants us to figure out a way to get to his spirit-cave and return with some kind of sacred hide."
"Knowing you, you'd just walk across the lava that's blocking the path, but you need to come up with some way across for 'lesser mortals' like us."
"You haven't yet talked to Jumu, the Jukari chief, about what it takes to get him to join your little crusade."
"Huitlapacti's dead, so Moctapotl and his Nahuatla will help you against the Myrmidex. Moctapotl's a gloomy Gus, but he sounds like he'll keep his word."

"Moctapotl, who's the deposed king of the Nahuatla, wants to be king again. Which means running Huitlapacti out of town, at the very least. Moctapotl thinks that Huitlapacti won't go without a big, bloody fight. Wish I had a tank or something."
"You don't yet know what it takes to get the Nahuatla king, what's-his-name, into your camp."

"The Tyrannosaurus Rex which was chewing on his little cousins, the Sakkhra, is dead of a terminal migraine. So the Sakkhra king Sysskarr will help on your mission... assuming you can understand anything he says."
"Sysskarr, who seems to be Top Lizard over there among the Sakkhra, wants you to kill the Thunderer, just an average Tyrannosaurus Rex who's driving down property values in lizard country."
"The leader of those Sakkhra lizard guys is named Sister. No, it was Sysskarr. We don't know yet what it is he'd want to help you out."
"We've already rescued the Urali statue, the Great Fabozz, from the cave where Darden the Huge stuck him."
"Your dear, dear friend Wamap of the Uralis wants you to rescue some blamed statue called the Great Fabozz from a cave. Big threat there, huh?"
"The last tribe on my list is the Urali. We don't know what their chief would want."
"That's the list, boss." Jimmy flips his notebook shut.

description.text:
a lean, dark-bearded man with kindly eyes.
*

items.text: "Yes, $P?"
"$P, I really need to talk to you about certain @problems we are facing.&
"I am Dr. Johann Spector, of course. Though my sanity has returned, my name remains the same.&
"No, please, just call me Johann.&
He sighs. "I have no job. I WAS an archaeologist. I seem to have botched that. And I've certainly abandoned my former role as Zipactriotl, self-serving shaman of the Nahuatla.&
"I no longer have any association with any tribe here. I somehow doubt the Nahuatla would want me back.&
"Now that my mind is clear, I see that there are many problems which face us with the Myrmidex.&
"These creatures are too great in number for any single band of men to defeat. I think we'll need to unite all the tribes in this land if we're to defeat the Myrmidex.&
"But just defeating them isn't enough. We must destroy their queen... else she will simply spawn a new generation of warriors to kill us.&
"And just destroying HER isn't enough. Somewhere in the Myrmidex caverns, there is an enormous black stone, like the small stones which transported us here.&
"This stone is throwing off bizarre, incredible energies which warp the flow of time in this valley. It could very well be that we are all trapped here until it is destroyed.&

"Even if we are not, and we find a way out, there's no telling what its presence could do. The Myrmidex might some day figure out how to tap its incredible power... which would be death to all humans here, and perhaps throughout the world.&
"The @stone in the @Myrmidex caves MUST be destroyed.&
"The Myrmidex caves house an enormous black stone possessing strange energies. It was these energies that drove me mad. The stone is dangerous and must be destroyed.&
"I think that the stone was originally set up in the Underground City of the Kotl. When the Kotl servants, the @Myrmidex, rebelled, they took the stone with them.&
"But the @Kotl generators managed to continue drawing power from the stone.&
"According to all I was able to grasp in the Underground City of the @Kotl, the Kotl deliberately bred the Myrmidex as a race of super-servants.&
"But the Myrmidex were too savage and escaped, carrying the black @stone with them.&
"The Kotl, who built the underground city, were a bipedal reptilian race descended from small, two-legged carnosaurs.&
"They had great mystical knowledge and were able to draw mystic power from the giant black @stone. They ran their city with this power.&
"They also used this power to breed themselves a race of servants, the Myrmidex. However, the Myrmidex became too savage to control, and escaped with the stone.&
"Fortunately for the Kotl, the mystic generators continued drawing power from the stones, even over this great distance.&

"It appears that the Kotl tried again, going out into the outer world and capturing representative human tribes from all over the world. Those tribesmen were the ancestors of the tribes living here today.&
"But men are just as aggressive as ants, and they, too, escaped to freedom.&
"It would seem that the Myrmidex returned to destroy their former masters, and drove the Kotl out of the Underground City, which sealed behind them.&
"It remained sealed until I, with my understanding of the ways of the power from the black stones, was able to open the doors. I didn't leave them open, as you found out. But you got in anyway.&
"The escaping Kotl appear to be the ancestors of today's Sakkhra.&
"Yes, we must unite the tribes. The tribes here follow the word of their chiefs, so we must go to each chief and persuade him to join this union.&
He shakes his head. "$P, I can never make up for what I've done if I drift around this valley. I want to accompany you and participate in fixing these problems. So I'm not going to leave you.&
"I'm already with you, $P.&
"Yes, yes. We'll talk later.&
"We'll talk later. But we MUST talk about certain @problems we face.&
"I don't grasp what you mean.&

description.text:
a stooped, fiftyish man who looks like a professor.
*

items.text: "$P! It's good to see you again! I had heard you were still alive, but I didn't know where you were."
"I see you haven't managed to find @Jimmy or @Aiela yet... that really should be one of our first priorities, you know."
"I see you have found Mr. Malone already. That's good. We should try to find @Aiela next."
"Now that you're here, it might be helpful to find the lab. There are several things there which will be very useful to us. It must be fairly close to the Kurak village."

"While I've been waiting for you to show up, I haven't been wasting my time here. In addition to my researches on these primitive cultures, I have also been thinking about ways to make some primitive weapons."
"I do hope it won't prove necesary, but if it should, ask me about @bombs and @rifles sometime."
"Yes, who?" He adjusts his spectacles, looks at you absent-mindedly. "Oh, it's my old friend $P."
"Eh? Eh? MY name? You've known my name for years. Professor Elliot Archimedes Rafkin, Ph.D., etc."
"Yes, $P, what is it?"
"Principally, I'm the curator of the local museum of natural history."
"Most recently, I've been the chief doctor and man of science in the village of the @Yolaru. I have spent much of my time studying the @tribes of this @valley."
Professor Rafkin nods. "Yes, this is my laboratory.
"Yes, there are many useful things there. I'm sure that it is somewhere south or southeast of the Kurak village."
"She had been captured by that ponderous fellow from the @Urali tribe.  Fortunately you managed to free her."
"I understand she was captured by the @Urali tribe. She seemed like a tough individual, but I hope she is all right. I hope we go and search for her soon."
"You know nearly as much about the Urali as I do, $P.  After all, you rescued Aiela from them. I never did get much chance to study their culture."

"From what I can make out, the Urali were thought to have disappeared for many years. They have only recently started raiding other villages, which leads me to suspect their village must be well-hidden."
"Local hunters have confirmed this supposition, saying that they have been trying to find them for some time. The raids seem to come from southeast of the Yolaru village, usually."
"This whole area in which we find ourselves is called the Valley of Eodon."
Prof. Rafkin points at Jimmy distractedly. "He's over there, $P."
"I have heard that he may be somewhere to the west of the Nahuatla, with a tribe called the @Disquiqui."
"There are many tribes here, my boy. Let us see, in alphabetical order: Barako, Barrab, @Disquiqui, @Haakur, Jukari, @Kurak, @Nahuatla, Pindiro, @Sakkhra, @Urali, and @Yolaru."
"From my studies of the tribesmen I've met, I believe that they were brought here from all over the world in ancient times."
"Their individual languages have obviously melded into one tongue, that which they all speak today."
"I haven't had time to do much research on that tribe yet."
"The Disquiqui are an interesting tribe. They seem to have broken away from the conflict-oriented tradition of many of the other groups."
"Their village lies west of the Nahuatla city."
"The Nahuatla men in this valley seem to be descended from the same race which developed into the Aztecs of central America."
"Their city, Tichticatl, is due south of the Yolaru village."
"The Haakur! Living examples of Neanderthal man, my boy! How I wish I could take one back with me to the museum."
"I suspect that the Kurak are descended from the first early pioneers who crossed the land bridge from Asia to North America... but it would take years of study to bear out this theory."
His eyes light up. "The Sakkhra! I have seen them. A race that exists nowhere in the fossil record, my boy! A bipedal reptilian race with an intelligence on a par with that of the human race!"
"A delightful tribe! Very civilized. I have lived among them since we came to the valley. Culturally, they have certain similarities to the ancient Kushites."
"Ah. Are you saying you want me to manufacture you a rifle? Just like that?"
"$P, are you asking me to build you a grenade?"
He makes a series of 'tsk,tsk' noises. "You want instructions on making gunpowder?"
He makes a series of 'tsk,tsk' noises. "You want instructions on making gunpowder?"
"Using tarred cloth strips on a branch would make an excellent torch."
"The best way to get charcoal would be to burn a @branch with a campfire or firepit."
"I'm sure you can pull branches from almost any tree."
"Potassium nitrate. Also called saltpeter. There was a bottle of it back at my @laboratory."
"Chances are good that most caves will have crystalline deposits, as well."
"You will need a hard clay pot to make grenades. That's simple to accomplish."
"If you can't find a hard clay pot, find a soft one and place it in a @kiln for a while."
"A large oven used for baking soft clay pots."
"You'll probably find sulphur pits in the vicinity of volcanoes.  You'll need a wire @screen of some kind to extract usable sulpher."
"It would have to be fairly tough wire screen. I think there was some back at the @lab that would work."
"A mortar. You know, a bowl used for grinding raw materials down into powder. NOT something for lobbing shells at the enemy."
"I had one back at the @lab."
"A grinding stone, or grindstone. You can find them by the dozens in native villages."
He scowls. "I most certainly will NOT leave. I was here first. Who do you think you are, ordering me about? Hmph."
"Um... my boy..." He looks timidly over the edge, into the water. "I hate to admit it... but I never learned to swim. For the time being, you're stuck with me."
"Ah, of course. The young learn all they think they can from the old, and then abandon them."
"Yes, a strip of cloth. You'll probably need a knife or scissors to cut one from a sheet of cloth."
"Any tar found in this land will undoubtedly be extremely hot. I would reccomend collecting it in a metal container of some kind. A bucket, perhaps."
"Ask the Nahuatla tribesman where to find some."
"You're welcome."
"I most certainly will NOT wait here. I'm a busy man. Things to do. Wait, indeed."
"Ummm... perhaps when we're on dry land."
"Oh, very well. Come back for me whenever you think I've languished here long enough." He scowls.
"Join what? Is something in need of repair?" He blinks owlishly. "Oh, you mean join YOU. I'm already with you."
"Sorry, $P, there's just too many people with you already."
"I'll join with you when you're on solid ground, $P."
"Oh, are we going somewhere?" He looks delighted. "Well, certainly. I've been HERE long enough."
Rafkin looks sheepish. "Er, yes. That's what the Yolaru call me. They offered to make me their shaman. I said that I'd be their Schweitzer instead."
"I was referring to Albert Schweitzer. He was a missionary in Africa. Doctor, writer, musician. A remarkable man."
"But the Yolaru took it as my title. 'Schweitzer: A special sort of shaman.' I didn't correct their misapprehension."
He smiles crookedly. "Oops."
"That's right, plumb my brains and then
ignore me.
abandon me for more interesting pursuits.
Humpf."
"Ask me about that later."
"Oh, very well. Let's see if you've brought me the proper parts."
"Well, good. I was busy thinking."
"To make a rifle, I'll need a length of iron-hard bamboo. Did you bring me some?"
"Good. Now we're cooking."
"Oh, too bad. I suppose I shall have to make it out of thin air. $P, go find some bamboo."
"To make a rifle, I'll need a length of iron-hard @bamboo, and I need to be in my @lab. We have to go there, first."
He sighs, exasperated. "$P, let me try to make you understand. Please don't make me use small words."
"None of us has a bamboo pole. Are you with me so far? Without a @BAMBOO POLE, I cannot make even a primitive rifle."
"Get me some bamboo, and I will construct you something that can arguably be called a rifle."
Using his tools, carefully and methodically, he drills a series of holes in the bamboo near one end.
With bits of string, loose finishing nails, and other interesting goods from his pockets and around the lab, he mounts a small piece of rock on the pole near one hole.
He mounts a small bit of metal on a short wooden rod, and attaches the middle of that rod to the bamboo pole so that the metal can swing into contact with the rock.
"What we end up with here," he explains, "is a sort of primitive, single-shot flintlock. To use it, pull this 'trigger', so that the other end strikes the flint."

"A spark will ensue. The spark will enter the pole through this hole here, and ignite the gunpowder which you will have packed into the tube. The gunpowder will propel your 'bullets', and voila, you have a functioning rifle."
As he has done for you in the past, Rafkin works on the bamboo pole, transforming it into a crude bamboo rifle.
"There." He looks up from his task. "Your bamboo pole is transformed into a lethal instrument of destruction." He hands back the transformed bamboo.
Then, he repeats the process with the other bamboo poles.
Then, he repeats the process with the other bamboo pole.
"I do not manufacture fully-loaded rifles, of course. I assume you know how to make @ammunition and load firearms."
"Oh, how unfortunate. Yes, I'm the gentle, sweet old Professor Rafkin. I teach young men archaeology and how to make bombs."
"Good! Imagine me, a man of education, having to manufacture munitions!"\
"To make some sort of crude grenade, you'll need the following ingredients:"
"A strip of cloth impregnated with @tar, to act as a fuse; five units of gunpowder; and a @hard clay pot."

"When you have these together, simply use the @strip of tarred cloth on the pot to seal the pot and act as a fuse.
What you end up with is a crude, but serviceable, bomb."
"The @gunpowder you're likely to be able to make may be very unstable stuff, so throwing the grenade at something could set it off."
"Alternatively, you can light the fuse and leave the thing behind. Then run like the dickens."
He sighs. "Professor Rafkin, Terrorist Teacher. That's me."
"Well... it's simple enough. You'll need a quantity of @charcoal, a quantity of @potassium nitrate, and a quantity of @sulphur."
"Put all these things in a @mortar or @grinding stone and grind them into powder. Gunpowder, that is."
"Then why did you ask? Hmph!"

"Since I've managed a rather clever variant on the classic muzzle-loader," he says proudly, "all you need to do is put the gunpowder into your bamboo rifle barrel, and you'll have a fully-loaded firearm."

a quiet man, almost more a jungle spirit than a man.

items.text: "Yes, friend $P?"
"It is $P! It has been long since Shamuru has seen you awake... long since the night that Darden the Huge trampled through our camp."
"Shamuru is the name the Barako @gave me."
"Shamuru is a tracker, a hunter, the best in all the valley."
"Shamuru enjoys traveling Eodon with $P."
"Shamuru also enjoys going to new places and exploring new things. If $P would like for Shamuru to @join with him, he has but to ask."
"Shamuru is an @adopted warrior of the Barako tribe. The Barakos live on the ledges to the north."
"Yes. Shamuru was not born to the Barakos. Indeed, Shamuru is more at home in the jungle than in the mountains where the Barakos live."
"Shamuru was found many moons ago wandering, naked and unarmed, his mind as clean as a baby's, in the high mountains above the Barako village."
"The Barakos took Shamuru in and made him a brother warrior. Shamuru does not remember his life before that time."
"I've never seen an Ankylosaur, I never hope to see one But this I will say anyhow - I'd rather see than be one."
"Your words..." He frowns. "Shamuru seems to see far-away things, places, people. Shamuru does not understand."
"You presume much, telling Shamuru to leave."
He shakes his head, smiling, and points at the water. "Shamuru will leave on land."
"If $P wishes. He can find Shamuru north of the Yolaru village... some of the time."
"You presume much, telling Shamuru to wait."
He shakes his head, smiling, and points at the water. "Shamuru would find it hard to wait on the water. Shamuru will wait to wait."
He nods briefly. "Shamuru will wait here. Do not forget him."
He gives you a slight smile. "Shamuru is with $P already."
"Shamuru will join with $P later, when he has fewer people traveling with him."
"Shamuru cannot join with $P now. Maybe later."
He considers briefly and nods. "Shamuru thinks it would be a good thing to travel with $P."
"A pleasure."
"Ask Dokray about that."
"Shamuru does not understand you."

items.text: He looks at you intently for several moments before speaking, as if trying to place your face.
"Triolo has heard of $P. $P's face is very familiar, somehow."
"Does $P need help with something?"
"Triolo is the name given me by the @Kuraks."
"Triolo is a shaman-in-training. The great shaman @Intanya is Triolo's teacher."
"Triolo's newest task is to follow $P around... and convey to him the will of the @spirits."

"Triolo belongs to the Kurak tribe. Triolo was not born a Kurak: Triolo came stumbling from the jungle, bereft of name and memory, many moons ago. Since then, @Intanya has taught Triolo the ways of the shaman."
"Triolo has learned only a small part of what Intanya knows. Small magics, but useful."
"Intanya, a great man, is shaman of the Kuraks. Triolo learns the spirit-magic of the shamans from him."
Triolo gestures towards Shamuru. "Shamuru is there."
"Shamuru is a hunter and tracker, of the @Barako tribe."
He looks puzzled. "Did $P mean shaman or shamuru?"
"Yopo is a mostly green plant used in many incantations."
"Pinde makes strong magics."
"Brown beans, very strong taste. Use it in spells."
"Used to invoke the spirits."
"That is the spirit of emotions, and strength."
"Motazz is the spirit of battle."
"That is the spirit of knowledge and visions."
Triolo gestures towards Aiela. "She is Aiela."
"Aiela has left our party. Triolo does not know where she has gone."
"Ah, the beauteous Aiela. Triolo has written songs about her."
"The evil Darden captured her, and holds her captive still. I am sure that were we to find where the Urali hide, we could free her."
"Barako village is close to the Kurak, but across the deep canyon of waters."
"Yes, Triolo sings. How did $P know that?"
He frowns. "$P's names call up images to Triolo's mind. Distant lands, faces with forgotten names. Perhaps $P is invoking a spirit of memory."
"The tribes war on one another while a terrible enemy, the @Myrmidex, kill them one by one. Intanya does all he can, but he cannot persuade the chiefs to unite."
"Myrmidex are like ants... but are the size of men. They are fierce meat-eaters."
"Leave? No, Triolo thinks he will stay here, and perhaps compose a tune."
He mimes as if he were going to dive off into the water, then laughs. "Perhaps Triolo will leave later, when meat-eating river fish do not surround him."
"As $P wishes. Triolo will return to Intanya and resume his studies until $P needs him again."
"Triolo waits for no man! Perhaps if a woman were to ask... A she-cat with a dimple in her smile... Triolo would wait for that."
He mimes as if he were going to dive off into the water, then laughs. "Perhaps Triolo will leave later, when meat-eating river fish do not surround him."
He sighs. "As $P wishes. Deny Triolo all the fun. Triolo will wait right here. Perhaps he'll compose a little song about $P. 'Breath like Sharptooth, nose like Longneck...'"
His eyes twinkle. He looks at you, behind you, behind him, under his arm. Finally, he looks down at himself and yelps. "$P! Triolo is already here."
"Triolo will join with $P later, when he has fewer people traveling with him."
"What? How can Triolo join with $P now? Maybe later."
"What? And give up Triolo's career?" He looks around him and grimaces. "Never mind, Triolo is with $P."
"$P should ask another about that."
"Very well, speak to Triolo later."
"Ask Shamuru about that."
"$P should ask another about that."

"You need a small blue stone for Topuru. Here."

"You need turtle bait to cross the Urali swamp. Here."

items.text: Dokray leans over and whispers into your ear: "Ugyuk is strongest and dumbest of all Haakur. Dokray and Ugyuk have fought many times. Dokray always wins, of course."
The Neanderthal sniffs the air.
The Neanderthal speaks in a deep, growling voice. "Smell new smell. Smell Dokray. Dokray bad. Dokray go away." The Neanderthal waves Dokray away, glowering at him, but does not go for his weapons.
The Neanderthal speaks in a grunting, gravelly voice: "Not know smell. New. Not like others. What want new smell?"
"Ugyuk smell $P."
"Bad Dokray is with $P. Does Ugyuk talk or smash?" His brow furrows. "Hurt to think. Ugyuk will talk."
"Ugyuk is name. Name is Ugyuk." He seems rather proud of the concept.
"Ugyuk. UG-YUK."
"Ugyuk strong. Smash skulls of lizards, enemies like @Dokray. Eat hearts. Become strongest." He demonstrates, pretending to smash his club into the skull of an imaginary beast. He pounds...
... and pounds ...
... and pounds.
"Ugyuk of Haakur tribe. Not know other tribes. Too many words. Too many names. New smell -- " he points at you -- "not from other tribes. Not from @Jukari. Jukari enemies."
"Haakur live where hills spit fire." He spits on your foot to demonstrate, and points at it. "But fire."
"Haakur chief @Grugorr. Grugorr."
"Dokray bad. Small, stupid. Always attack Ugyuk. Ugyuk always smash Dokray's brains." He waves his hands to mime his club coming down and someone's brains flying in all directions.
Dokray speaks up: "Ugyuk lies! Dokray always smashes Ugyuk. $P, let Dokray smash Ugyuk NOW."
"Ugyuk not know. Words like what chief say. Chief @Grugorr."
"Grugorr chief Haakur."
"Bug bug bug!
"No my dear boy, those aren't bugs. They are simply another feature of this valley, which I'm documenting thoroughly."
Ugyuk stares blankly at the professor for a moment, then resumes "Big bug-things. Bad. More bad than @Dokray."
Big bug-things. Bad. More bad than @Dokray."
"No, Ugyuk stay. This is place of Ugyuk."
He looks nervously at the water. "Later. Leave later. No go in water. Water make clean. Make Ugyuk weak to be clean."
"Good. Ugyuk tired of people." He turns away to leave.
"Ugyuk wait here. Or go other place."
He looks nervously at the water. "Later. Wait later. No go in water. Water make clean. Make Ugyuk weak to be clean."
He thinks about it for a while. (A long while.)
His brow furrows.
His head begins to shiver.
A thought finally intrudes where none had been before. His eyes open wide. "Yes! Wait here. Ugyuk wait here. Come back for Ugyuk later."
He has to think about that for a while.
He thinks about it for a while longer.
Finally: "Ugyuk did that already."
"Jukari! Men. Live near Haakur. Have many @sparklies."
"Sparklies. Sparklies!" He gestures, pretending to hold something small up to his ears, nose, neck... "Sparkly rocks."
Prof. Rafkin speaks up: "I think, my boy, that he's referring to diamonds. Diamond jewelry."
Ugyuk nods vehemently. "Yes. What he say."
The Neanderthal shrugs and turns away.
"Ugyuk not know. Is good to eat?"
Ugyuk points at Dokray. "Not join. Bad Dokray with. Not help Bad Dokray. Make Dokray go, Ugyuk will join."
"No. Ugyuk will not join. Too many people with $P now."
"Ugyuk cannot join $P now! Too wet!"
"Go with? Will go with. Ugyuk join, protect. Smash heads of enemies."
Ugyuk bristles and prepares himself for combat. "Well?" persists Dokray. "Let Dokray smash Ugyuk!"
"Bad Dokray! Bad Dokray! Ugyuk will smash all!"
Dokray's face falls. He turns back to Ugyuk. "Later," he suggests, "when new friends are not here, Dokray will smash Ugyuk's face into new shape."
Ugyuk snarls. "Bring whole tribe," he suggests, then turns back to you.

description.text:

items.text: The statue says nothing. (Neither would you, with your head missing!)
"Greet-ings. Wel-come to the @Ci-ty of the Kot-l."
"The ci-ty is ac-tive. I see the @gen-er-a-tors are func-tion-ing."
The automoton looks at the silver figure seated next to him. "How-ev-er, I see that some of the guar-di-an ser-vants have bro-ken down."
Jimmy breaks in: "So that's a guard? Sorta like an Argent Sergeant, eh?"
"I see you are a hu-man. In the ab-sence of con-tra-dic-to-ry or-ders from my mas-ters, I will join your par-ty and serve you. How may I ac-com-mo-date you?"
"How may I serve you?"
"I am Yu-na-pot-li. I know it is my name for I re-mem-ber it."
The automaton pauses for a moment, as if thinking. "I would re-mem-ber much more, if I had my @brain."
"My oc-cu-pa-tion is that of ser-vant. E-ver since the hu-mans left, I and @o-thers like me have served the @Kot-l."
"E-ver since the Kot-l @left, I have been the guar-di-an of the doors to the ci-ty. It is my job to @swing the doors o-pen and closed."
"Ma-ny of my me-mo-ries were im-bued in the crys-tal brain which you re-turned to me."
"Yes, ma-ny of my me-mo-ries are not with-in me. They are im-bued in a crys-tal brain. I be-lieve the brain is some-where with-in the Ci-ty of the Kot-l."
"If you find my brain and give it to me, I will know more things than I do now."
"It was the Kot-l who cre-a-ted me. They were wise be-ings. They were not hu-mans. They were rep-tiles."
"They once had hu-mans as ser-vants. That is why I am shaped as a hu-man, for I am a ser-vant. But the Kot-l are gone now; they @left."
"@Kat-al-kot-l knows ma-ny things about the Kot-l. You should speak with him."
"There are o-ther au-to-ma-tons like my-self with-in the Ci-ty of the Kot-l. They are not so in-tel-li-gent as I. I have no i-dea what they have been do-ing since the Kot-l left and I fell a-sleep."
"The doors to the city are al-rea-dy o-pen!"
"Do you wish me to o-pen the doors to the ci-ty?"
"Yes, the Kot-l left a long long time a-go. The @Myr-mi-dex at-tacked them. I do not re-mem-ber why. Per-haps you should ask @Kat-al-kot-l."
"When they left, they placed me at the doors. I was to ad-mit a-ny Kot-l or a-ny-one with peace-ful in-tent. They left the @gen-er-a-tors run-ning so that the ci-ty would be pleas-ant."
"But much la-ter some men came and took my head so I could not think. It has ob-vi-ous-ly been re-att-ached."
"The last thing I re-mem-ber is one of the hu-mans reach-ing for my head."
"The Myr-mi-dex are gi-ant in-sects. They are sa-vage and re-pel-lant. I do not re-mem-ber much a-bout them. Per-haps you should ask @Kat-al-kot-l."
"This is the Ci-ty of the Kot-l, built long long a-go be-fore hu-mans came or Myr-mi-dex came. Now I think no one lives here."
"The Ci-ty of the Kot-l was built long a-go be-fore hu-mans came or Myr-mi-dex came. Now I think no one lives there."
"Kat-al-kot-l is ve-ry wise. He stands in the cen-ter of the Great Pla-za of the Ci-ty. He an-swers many quest-ions."
"But he can-not move and can-not touch a-ny-thing."
"Hu-mans. Hu-mans were once the ser-vants of the Kot-l, I think. You should ask @Kat-al-kot-l."
"The ci-ty is pow-wered by migh-ty gen-er-a-tors."
"You should ask @Kat-al-kot-l a-bout them. He would know more than I."
"But you can-not see them now for the doors to the ci-ty are closed."
"The Kot-l cre-at-ed man-y in-ter-est-ing de-vices. When the @Myr-mi-dex at-tacked, they al-so cre-at-ed @weap-ons and @arm-or to help de-fend the ci-ty."
"One you may find in-ter-est-ing is a de-vice to help @lo-cate the black stone the Myrm-i-dex took."
"Most de-vic-es should still func-tion. You may use an-y you find."
"It is a round ob-ject with a light which in-di-cates a path towards the black stone."
"You may find a long black staff. It caus-es great dam-age a-gainst the Myr-mi-dex."
"They also found a gas that was ve-ry eff-ect-ive a-gainst the Myr-mi-dex. It is found in large green can-is-ters."
"Kot-l ar-mor would not fit you. But they cre-at-ed a ve-ry good shi-eld that you could use."
"I know the Kot-l cre-at-ed heal-ing crys-tals that could al-so heal hu-mans."
"But I can-not.
I have o-pened the doors to the ci-ty. Now it is my du-ty to be your guide."
It is my du-ty to stay with you and open the @doors to the ci-ty."
"I am al-rea-dy with you, sir."
"De-light-ed to speak with you. I hope we will talk a-gain soon."
"Ve-ry well, I shall not."
"Ve-ry well, I shall o-pen them for you."
The automaton closes its eyes with a 'clack' and appears to concentrate. There is a grinding noise from the direction of the doors...
His eyes 'clack' open. "There! It is done."
The automaton takes the crystal brain from $Y. A door opens in the side of the golden head, and Yunapotli places the brain inside its skull.
"Thank you. I am now much smart-er. I now know a-bout man-y @de-vic-es that the Kot-l dev-el-oped to com-bat the @Myr-me-dex."

description.text:
