description.text:
an intense looking man in native clothing.
*

items.text: He looks over your clothing with a surprised expression. "Blessings of the spirits on the stranger. May I help you with something?"
"Hello again, $P. I hope the spirits have been kind."
"I am Paxaptamac."
"I make fine ornaments and feathered robes of the best @cloth."
"Normally I would be able to @trade with you for something, but I recently finished a large feathered cloak, and my stock is depleted."
"This is the Nahuatla tribe.  Most civilized of all the tribes."
He grins at you. "Best dressed, too."
"As I said, I recently sold my last cloak, and it will take quite some time for me to make another... even if I had the @feathers I need."

"I use only the finest parrot feathers. When I was younger, I could go out and hunt parrots myself. A few minutes work on a dead parrot with my knife, and I could usually find several usable feathers."
He looks at you thoughtfully for a moment.
"If you were to bring me feathers, I would trade with you for them. One emerald for ten feathers."
"I will trade you one emerald for 10 parrot feathers."
"Using a loom on flax will produce cloth."
"I sometimes use blue stones in my ornaments. The @Barrab seem to have many of them."
"The Barrab live somewhere to the west, I hear."
He shakes his head. "I do not use any bones in my work."
"Cloth made from good @flax is wonderfully easy to work with. Soft, easily sewn, easily decorated. Much better than the simple @hides some tribes use."
"@Yucca plants are a good source of flax, though it can be quite tedious to collect enough for a good garment."
"Most of them have reddish orange flowers. There are a couple out behind my shop."
"Many of the more primitive tribes use hides as clothing. I find @cloth much easier to work with."
"King Moctapotl is once again upon the throne. He was in exile, but when we found that Huitlapacti was truly mortal..." he shudders.
"Huitalpacti will trouble none of us again."
He looks at you with great concern. "Stranger, that is a name that none should speak in Tichticatl."
"I have heard of the Myrmidex, but I have never seen one. I hope I never do!"
"Huitalpacti is dead, at last. The Nahuatla are happier for his passing."
He frowns and looks at the ground. "All hail the king."
"May the spirits follow you, $P."
"I do not understand what you say."
"I see you have some feathers, $Y... would you like to sell them to me?"
"Ah, good!  Let me see just how many you have brought for me."
"Ah well," he sighs. "Perhaps another time, then."
"You do not have even 10 feathers for me. When you have more than 10, we can discuss trading again."
"Will you take #2 emerald\s for your #1 feathers?"
"That's the best price I can offer. Perhaps another day. What else can I help you with?"
"Good!" He collects the feathers and gives you #2 emerald\s.

description.text:
a germanic man wearing worn modern clothes.
*

items.text: Cautiously, he waits for you to speak.
He eyes you suspiciously. "It's Seggalion."
"I don't know if I should tell you or not..."
"I'm searching for @diamonds."
"I knew I shouldn't have told you! Now you'll try to get them first!"
He looks at you suspiciously. "You're not looking for modules, are you?"
"I've met him, a time or two. What's it to you?"

He looks askance at Shamuru.
"Never heard of him. Nope. Never."
"He looked familiar... I've seen that face before, somewhere."
He glares at you angrily. "That's NOT my name!"
He shudders, as though from a bad memory. "That was a terrible place. Never did like dogs, anyway."
"I don't know anyone named Fritz."

"Work.... work.... The greatest joy is work....."

"Arbeit macht frei!"
"Ah... I have heard of the Great And Powerful Allston."
"If you ain't Steve, you ain't shit."
"Don't listen to him, he's always putting words in people's mouths!"
"Squawrk!"
"Love those wiper-weasels!"
"Bob? He said something about getting some sleep. I wouldn't disturb him... he had a gun."
"Go, Oilers!&
"Jason? He's fired!"
"Get back to work!"
"Glen? What? He still owes me money!"
"Goodbye. Leave me in peace."
"What are you talking about?"
"Please, leave me alone."
"Go away, leave me alone."
"Now go... get out of here."

description.text:
a rugged-looking native dressed in bear skins.
*

items.text: "It is $P, who saved young Halisa! Welcome."
The native stares at you: Not rudely, but cautiously. "Another @stranger in Barako lands."
"Member of Barako tribe."
"Barako." The native seems to warm to the subject. "We live in the mountains and protect ourselves from the cold with heavy furs."
"We war with the @Pindiro. There are also @strangers in our lands, strangers who are not enemies."
"Our ruler is @Halawa, a queen of great wisdom and cunning. Our greatest warrior is @Shamuru."
"Halawa is ruler of the Barako. Her mother was queen before her. It is our way: The Barako have queens instead of kings."
"@Halisa is to be the next queen... if she lives so long." The native looks unhappy.
"Halisa has spoken much of the kindness of her rescuer, oh $P."
"Too much said already. Go speak to the queen if you would learn more."
"$N knows little of the Barako shaman. He has been gone for many, many days. $N fears he may not return."
The native bows to Shamuru. "The great hunter is with you now."
Shamuru nods in return. "Shamuru will be travelling with $P for some time; tell the others of the tribe."
"As Shamuru wishes."
"Shamuru is the name of the greatest hunter of the Barako. Shamuru travels the valley, learning all of its paths and secrets. Shamuru is more at home in the wild than with his tribe."
"Do you mean @Shaman or @Shamuru?"
"There are two strangers in these lands. One is @old and the other @young. Which did you mean?"
"On an island west of the Barako village lives an old man named Topuru. Topuru is mad, always speaking of rocks. He stays away from the Barako."
"In the northeast part this valley lives a strange man -- strange like you. His furs are odd and he speaks oddly."
"He says his name is Frit-azz. There is much more to his name but it is impossible to remember. He says he comes from far away."
"The Pindiro live north and east of us, by a lake. They live on the plains and hunt plains-beasts."
"May the spirits save you from falling."
"I know not of $Z."

description.text:
a somewhat Asian-looking native in heavy furs.
*

items.text: "Speak; this one will listen."
"This one's name is $N."
"$N hunts and gathers for the Barrab tribe, dwellers of the @mesa."
"$N belongs to the Barrab tribe, dwellers on the @mesa. Our chief is @Balakai, and @Nakai is our prince. The Barrabs are enemies of the @Sakkhra."
"Balakai is chief of the Barrab, and shaman. Balakai's wisdom is great."
Quietly the native says "She is about here, somewhere."
"There are three mesas in the western parts of the valley. One is the Mesa of the Barrab, where this one lives. North of our village is the Lesser Mesa, where no one lives and little grows."
"Further north is the Great Mesa, largest of the three, where only beasts and plants live."
The native's face loses all expression. "Such things are best discussed with the Barrab chieftain, who is @Balakai."
"Ah! Sakkhra. Lizards in the shape of men. Fierce warriors indeed. Sakkhra and Barrab have been enemies for many generations."
"Sakkhra dwell in caves west of the Great Mesa. Once they dwelt further north. $N does not know why the Sakkhra left their ancient caves for their new dwellings."
"$N has heard of the Myrmidex. Fierce beasts to the far east. $N has heard that when the eastern tribes fall, the Myrmidex will next come for the Barrab and the @Sakkhra."
"$N knows of the Barrab warrior named Nawl. $N thinks it is best that Nawl keep well away from the Barrab mesa. Nawl is both a braggart and a fool."
"Nakai is son of the chieftain, Balakai."
"Nakai is sorely ill. Nakai may soon die of illness."
"That is something to speak of with the @chieftain, not with this poor, humble one."
"$N bids fare well."
"$N knows anguish, for $N does not understand those words."
"Ah." The native beams. "$N was certain it was so. Welcome is the mighty $P among the Barrab."
"Oh." The native looks faintly confused. "$N was in error."
"... as the mighty $P already knows."
"But surely this is already known. Is $N not addressing the mighty $P, who cured Balakai's son @Nakai?"
"Nakai was sorely ill, but was saved by the actions of a stranger."
"$N is speaking to that noble stranger."
"Is $N not addressing that stranger?"

description.text:
a bleary-eyed, drunken-looking (and -smelling) native.
*

items.text: "Oh, another (hic!) visitor, like @Moctapokl. Hi!"
"(Hic!) Yesh?"
"Ny mame is $N. At leasht, it was this morning."
"$N doesn't have one of those." $N looks puzzled, trying to figure out what a 'job' is.
"Thish is the Disquiqui tribe. Our chief is @Chafblum and our shaman is @Larrifin. Disquiqui are the greatesht of the tribes."
"We make war on no one. But we DO have a prisoner. $N doesn't know how we got a prisoner without making war, but we did. Its name is @Jim-my."
"Our chaf is Chiefblum. Uh, our chief is Chafblum. (Hic!) Strong warrior, mighty leader. Chafblum is around the feasht shomewhere."
"Moctapickle? Oh, yes... that sad Nahuatla king.
He stayed here for a while. Never drank enough. Was always sad about something."
He's always sitting around in the village, moaning about his exile or something. He's no fun."
"Oh, yes, we Disquiqui are the best paddle makers. Many people use our paddles, some even use them with rafts!  We use them for making pulque. Have to. Make lots of @pulque."
"Pulque is good drink. Very good drink. Very very good drink. Pulque almost like food, but better."
"Disquiqui shaman is called Larrifin. Larrifin is very good shaman. Though he does not know anything about healing. Or invoking the spirits."
"Guoblum's mate-to-be has a name like that. Skinny, noisy warrior from far away."
"Skinny? SKINNY? Why, I oughta --"
"Oh, there Jimmy is."
"$N thinks he is in hut in Disquiqui village somewhere. Look around." The native vaguely waves in the direction of the village.
"Oh, you were boring anyway."
"Who is $Z?"

items.text: It grunts: "Uhhh. Uhhh."

"Haakur." It slaps itself. "Haakur tribe."

description.text:

*

items.text: "$P, who returned to us the sacred hide, is welcome in Jukari lands."
"Beware, stranger: This is Jukari land."
"$N gathers food for the Jukari tribe, and protects the young and weak from the @Haakur."
"$N is of the Jukari tribe. We live in the land of the shaking earth, where @rock flows like water and the spirits are fiercest."
"We have no shaman. Old shaman crushed by stones. Must have failed to please mountain spirits."
"The Haakur are ugly men living to the northeast. They live in caves and are brutes."
"Rock that flows from the mountains, glows at night. Killed our old @chief.  There are also pools of hot @sulphur.&
"The new chief is named Jumu. Jumu's father Kumaru died under a flow of hot rock, mere days ago."
"There are diamonds in this land. But that is a question for the chief."
"There are pits of sulphur in this land. Travel about and you will find them."

description.text:

items.text: "Hail, $P.&
"$P may call me $N.&
"$N is a member of the @Kurak tribe.&
"$N helps to search for @Aiela, who has been captured by the Urali tribe.&
"We are the Kuraks. We are one with the jungle. We are the greatest tribe, for great are our enemies, the @Yolaru and the @Myrmidex.&
"And recently, the @Urali.&
"There is none here. $N believes there is some to the southeast, east of the stone city of the @Nahuatlas.&
"The Nahuatla are a foolish tribe who live away from the spirits; they build their huts of stone and cover the earth with more stone. Their village is all of stone. It is to the southeast.&
"It is easy to make hides. $P must find a mighty beast of the jungle and slay it in single combat. Then he must use his knife on its carcass to cut free its hide.&
"Yolaru are fierce black warriors, noble in combat, a fit and proper enemy for the Kuraks. They live to the east of the Kuraks.&
$N scowls. "The Myrmidex are no fit enemy. They are insects the size of warriors. They are fierce and treacherous.&
"They live only to kill, and may only be killed; they know no thought or reason. Their nest is close to the Kurak village, to the west.&
"$N has heard of one with a name such as that. He is a prisoner in the village of the Disquiqui, to the far southwest. He awaits marriage to the chief's daughter Guoblum.&
"Not any more, pal! Super-Bachelor is free once again.&
"Why, that young whippersnapper! Running off to get himself married when there are IMPORTANT things to do. I'd like to give him a piece of my mind.&
$N starts to speak, but...

... Prof. Rafkin cuts $N off.
"Not nice to talk about someone right in front of his face, my boy. At least wait for me to turn my back, so you can talk behind it.&
"$N has heard of one such. A wise man of the Yolaru. They call him their @schweitzer.&
$N shrugs. "$N does not know what that word means, either.&
"$N knows of the Urali. They live far away, to the southeast.&
"It was Urali warriors who had taken Aiela away. But $P has rescued our princess.&
"No one knows where they live. Except for the mad one, @Topuru.&
$N's face settles into an angry, determined look. "But they have our princess, Aiela. They will return her, and they will pay.&

"$N has heard the story of one called Topuru. Topuru is supposed to be one of the @Urali, but a madman. Topuru lives near the Barako, across the deep river canyon to the north, on a little island, all alone.&
"Aiela is princess of the Kuraks, most beautiful woman of the tribe. She is held by Darden the Huge, chief of the @Urali tribe.&
"$P knows well who Aiela is. Aiela is princess of the Kuraks. $P rescued her from Darden the Huge, chief of the Urali.&
"$P knows well who Aiela is. Aiela is $P's mate. $P rescued her from Darden the Huge, chief of the Urali.&
Aiela chimes in, teasingly: "$P suffered many blows in rescuing Aiela. Perhaps $P's memory is not what once it was.&
"There is a legend that once all the tribes were united for a time.&
"A warrior called Oloro-of-No-Tribe brought the tribes together to fight the lizards of the jungle when the lizards were too numerous and too deadly.&
"Oloro went from chieftain to chieftain. By his strength and spirit Oloro persuaded each chief to join his union.&
"Then Oloro built a great drum to summon all the tribes together. Oloro beat upon the drum and all the tribes came, slaying the lizards. Thus were the tribes united... once.&
"May the spirits guard your path, $P.&
"$N does not understand your words, $P.&

items.text: "Yes? What do you wish of me, outsider?&
"My name only pales beside yours, oh $P, conquerer of Huitlapacti, restorer of Moctapotl.&
"I am $N.& The native looks alarmed by your foreign appearance and manner.
"I am a citizen of Tichticatl. I tend the fields, transport grain, work on @crafts, elude the @thunder-lizards and @Myrmidex in the field; we all do.&
"I am a faithful servant of the king @Moct -- er, @Huitlapacti.&
"Atlipacta is our swordmaker. She has a shop just west of the main plaza where the sundial sits.&
"Yes, there is supposed to be bamboo growing thick, some ways to the east of Tichticatl.&
"Emeralds are highly prized in Tichticatl.&
"I am a citizen of the Nahuatla, the builders of this great city of Tichticatl.& The native's gesture takes in the entire city.
"Bones. Have I not heard of some great collection of bones? Yes. North of the giant @bamboo stand, there is a place where the @thunder-lizards go to die. There you can find bones.&
$N spits. "That for the memory of Huitlapacti.&
"All hail our new king Huitlapacti.& The native's voice is fearful.
"Many of us make @pots sometimes. We have a fine @weapon maker in Tichticatl, and our @weaver makes very nice clothes and ornaments.&
"Paxaptamac the weaver lives a short distance west of the pyramid of the sun.&
"Many of us own nice pots. You could make your own, if you were to use some @clay to form it, then fire it in a @kiln.&
"One can get clay from the riverbanks, with a @digging stick.&

The native looks slightly puzzled.
"Yes, a digging stick. A small stick specially carved digging roots and clay.&
"There is a kiln along the south edge of Tichticatl.&
"The tall stone structure at the eastern end of Tichticatl. There is a sun-dial at it's peak.&
"You know -- the great lizards of the jungle and the field.&
"This native is collectively referring to dinosaurs and other prehistoric reptiles, $P. DO pay attention.&
The native looks puzzled, but does not comment.
"You know, dummy: Dinosaurs.&
The native looks puzzled, but does not comment.
"It sounds as though you wish to see the weapon-maker, Atlipacta. She crafts weapons in a shop near the palace, just west of the pyramid of the sun.&
"You speak of our king, whom you yourself restored to the throne.&
The native hesitates and looks fearful. "I do not know that name. NO ONE in Tichticatl knows that name. Do you understand?&
"The Myrmidex? Evil monsters from the northwest. They are like ants the size of a man, and they attack us without mercy. The fields are no longer a safe place to work.&
"I have heard of the Urali. They are a savage race. They raid Tichticatl, coming in from the northeast, but I know not where they live.&
"May the spirits guide you.&
"I do not understand your words. What is a '$Z'?&
"Good.&
The native looks nervously all around to see if anyone is listening, then leans in close.
"The new king, Huitlapacti, has decreed that no one say that name. It is the name of the old king.&
"To speak that name is death, for the old king is alive, living out in the jungle somewhere, planning his return. This is why the name is not to be spoken.&

, enemies of the @Barako
"The Pindiro queen is named Inara."

"Logs, tied together. Must have four people with @paddles to use raft."

The native shrugs, not understanding.

description.text:
a sallow-skinned, suspicious-eyed native.

items.text: The native stays at a safe distance and remains cautious. "What does the stranger want?"
The native gives you a cautious, appraising look; then a broad smile breaks out on the native's face. "It is you, the $P one who slew @Darden. You are a friend to Urali. Ask what you will of me."
"My name is pale and weak beside yours, oh $P. I do not wish to utter it and be ashamed. Let it be enough that I am one of the Urali."
The native laughs. "To ask one of the Urali his name is foolishness. I would never tell you my name. Why should I give you power over me? I am one of the Urali. That is enough."
"I hunt, and fish, and gather plants to eat; I harvest our lovely swamp, as do all @Urali."
"We are the Urali. Mighty in war. Defended and fed by our mother, the swamp, which is bountiful to the Urali, dangerous to all @others."
"We Urali know all the @trails and paths through the swamp, which you would never find."
"Wamap
"@Darden
is our chieftain."
"You do not need to know our secret trails, oh $P. You are already friend of the Urali and have nothing to fear here."
"First I must know: Are you a @friend of Darden the Huge, or Darden's @enemy?"
"The Great Fabozz is a spirit of the Valley of Eodon. His are the virtues of courage and strength as the animals possess them."
"It is the Great Fabozz who commands the Mighty Lizard which guards the pathway to the Urali village.
But our @statue of Fabozz has been taken by @Darden the Huge.
"I know you are the friend of the Urali. If you were not, you would not have slain Darden the Huge."
"If you are the friend of @Darden the Huge, you do not need to speak to one so lowly as I." The native gives you an ugly look and turns away from you.
"I do not understand you."
The native looks at you closely and suspiciously. "I do not know why, but I believe you. So I will tell you."
"A path runs from the entrance to Urali lands, through our village, and to the cave where Darden lives and keeps Darden's prisoners. Do not follow it; it is well-manned by Urali guards."
"Instead, go west until you reach the swamp water and turn south from there. Travel south holding close to the water."
"Follow the swamp as it curves and twists, until you are moving north again. Soon you will come upon a guarded cave opening."
"It is there that you will find Darden and those @Darden holds @prisoner. This path will lead you secretly past most guards; only at the cave mouth, perhaps, will you confront guards."
"I do not understand you."
"You cannot be neither! You are either Darden's @friend or Darden's @enemy!"
"Darden the Huge. The old chief died childless, so his sister's son Darden became chief, not long ago."
"He was evil and cruel. But now things are better. Darden is dead."
The Urali looks at you suspiciously.
"Few wanted him to be chief. But ever since Darden imprisoned @Fabozz, the Urali are in Darden's power."
"Since Darden became chief, it is fighting, always fighting. Darden tells the Urali to raid into the lands of @other tribes, else Darden will set the Mighty Lizard upon Darden's own warriors!"
"It is bad. Here is all the Urali could ever want. The Urali never want to leave, even to fight @other tribes. Now we must raid, we must kill, we must take @prisoners."

"The Myrmidex are beasts, more savage than any man, or even Urali. They live far away from the Urali. But they will come for the Urali some day. It would be good if tribes would @unite to fight them. The Myrmidex are too fierce for the Urali."
"Do you speak of Darden's prisoner @Aiela, or his spirit-prisoner, the Great @Fabozz?"
"Darden stole the statue of the Great @Fabozz. It commands the Mighty Lizard which guards the Urali village."
"Darden told the Urali that Darden would make the Mighty Lizard destroy the Urali if Darden were not made chieftain. So we made him chief." The native sounds sad.
"@Darden used his big riding lizard to take the statue deep into the cave, where light could not reach. Many warriors have brought light to Fabozz, but our torches and fires are not enough."
The native brightens. "But that is all over. The Great Fabozz is once again where he belongs, thanks to you."
The native looks at you curiously. "You look as strong as a warrior, but strange, like a spirit-made-flesh. Perhaps you could rescue the Great Fabozz. Would you?"
"There is tar here, in the swamp valley. On the west side of the swamp water, south of the land bridge that leads to the Urali village, is a great tar pit."
"Topuru was one of the Urali once, shaman to the Urali. Topuru angered the shaman of a faraway tribe and was driven mad. I have never seen him since."
"I do not understand you."
"You wish to rescue the Great @Fabozz?"
"I do not know many of the tribes. Outside our swamp valley, nearby, there are the Yolaru to the north; they are black-skinned warriors, very fierce."
"Beyond them, to the northwest, there are the Kurak, cunning in the forests."
"South of the Yolaru, there are the Nahuatla, who build their city of stone."
"And west of the Nahuatla, down below, are the Disquiqui, who fight poorly but live merry lives."
"There are more tribes besides those, but I do not know them."
"Unite the tribes? If it can be done, it is for the chiefs to decide."
"Since Darden is dead, our chief is the shaman Wamap. Travel the swamp and speak to all; you will find Wamap."
"@Darden is our chief, but Darden will never help another tribe. While Darden lives, the tribes may never be united."
"Aiela, Princess of the Kuraks. @Darden coveted her. Darden captured and imprisoned her."
"But you have freed her."
"Aiela is kept in a cave in the south of the swamp. You need to know about the @path."
"May the spirits protect you... so long as you do not seek to harm the Urali."
"I do not understand you."
"And you have likewise restored Fabozz to the Urali, so the Urali are again free."
"But @Fabozz remains away from the Urali, so the Urali can not truly be free."
The native sighs. "I have asked too much of you. I should know better. And Fabozz must remain a prisoner in Fabozz' cavern @prison."
The native brightens. "Yes? Yes? I will tell you how."
"In the center of our village is a circle of fires. There we talk to the Great Fabozz, and sometimes we are honored to have him talk to the Urali."
"@Darden took the Great Fabozz from that place and into a deep cave at the northern end of the swamp. Now we cannot reach him."
"Until the Great Fabozz is returned to his rightful place, the Urali are prisoners, not free men and women. Without our spirit, we are less than true Urali."
"If you would free the Great Fabozz, go far back into that cave in the north of the swamplands, and move the Great Fabozz back onto his circle of fire, where the sun may shine on him again."
The native sighs. "I have asked too much of you. I should know better. And Fabozz must remain a prisoner in his cavern @prison."

items.text: "What does warrior from beyond want?"
"$N is member of Yolaru tribe. There are many @other tribes.&
"$N is warrior and gatherer of food, as are all Yolaru.&
"Iron bamboo? South of place of bones.&
"You want bone? Easy to find.  Go south from Yolaru village. Walk at bottom of cliff. You will find place of many bones. Do not enter caves. Dangerous animals there.&
"Anyone can get hide. Kill large beast. Use knife on body. Then have hide.& The Yolaru looks contemptuous of your ignorance in this matter.
"Have heard of such. @Disquiqui have it.&
Jimmy breaks in: "Not any more, they don't!"
"Disquiqui HAD it.&
"Nahuatla call their stone city Tichticatl. One day's travel south of Yolaru village.&
"Disquiqui. Stupid tribe. Drink, sing all time.&
"Find Disquiqui? Go to city of stone where @Nahuatla live. Take path south to foot of cliff. Go west. Find Disquiqui there.&
"Warrior of @Nahuatla. Once chieftain there. Have heard he lives with @Disquiqui now.&
"Antlike beast. Strong, fierce, hungry, evil. Yolaru hate Myrmidex more than anything. But cannot beat Myrmidex. Myrmidex always win.&
"Rafkin came to our tribe. We captured. Was not angry, did not fight. Showed us healing. Showed us many things.&
"We said, 'You will be our shaman.' He said, 'No, your shaman is good. I will be your schweitzer.' We do not know what schweitzer is, but Rafkin is our @schweitzer.&
"You wish to speak to our schweitzer, who is called @Rafkin?"
"He is in Yolaru village. Find him there.&
"Tuomaxx. Drum-maker. Disquiqui sent him away. He was strange.&
"You want him? Follow path south from Yolaru village. Keep to the west, and you should find a hill.  Tuomaxx lives there.&
"Urali warriors. Attack, steal women from all tribes. Only since Darden the Huge became chief there. When they attack Yolaru village, always come from east or southeast.&
"You wish to unite tribes?" The warrior looks doubtful. "Too long fighting. Do not think you can. Speak to @chiefs if you wish to try. I am not chief.&
"Yolaru chief is Apaton. Find him in Yolaru @village.&
"Yolaru village is north of stone city of @Nahuatla. Find stone city, go north. Cannot fail to see it.&
"You want drum? Find @Tuomaxx.&
"Chief of @Urali. Big, evil. Mighty warrior.&
"There are many tribes in valley. $N's tribe is Yolaru. Nearby are Kurak and @Disquiqui, pale-skins, and @Nahuatla, with skin like copper.&
"Farther away... @Urali. Pindiro. Barrab. Barako. Jukari. Haakur, ugly men. Sakkhra, lizards who walk like men. Do not know much about these tribes.&
"Do not know YOUR tribe at all.&
"Fare well. Watch out for great lizards.&
"Cannot help you.&
"Cannot help you. Ask the @schweitzer.&
"There he is.& The Yolaru bows respectfully to Rafkin.
"Greetings, $N. Good to see you again.&

items.text: "Once more 'you' of Earth address 'I' of the Xorinite dimension."
"At this progression point in the temporal continuity, how do 'you' wish to be addressed?"
"'$9'. A series of vocal sounds serving as a temporary referent for 'you'. Very well. Does '$9' recall previous conversations with 'me'?"
"Excellent. This obviates the need for reiteration of previous declarations of origin, intent, and activity. What shall 'we' speak of?"
"Unfortunate. Repetition of previously-discussed information required. 'You' must sometime learn to extend perception along 'your' temporal continuity to avoid such confusion."
"The manifestation before 'you' is a life-form projection from the Xorinite dimension."
"'I' of Xorinia communicate with  the bipedal organic units of Earth through this projection."
"'I' observe activity at various points along Earth's temporal axis. In wealthier dimensions 'I' trade information, but 'you' of Earth have never offered any of significant value."
"'My' projections are at this point in space time primarily to allow 'me' to observe and analyze the surrounding space-time @anomaly. What do 'you' wish to know, '$9'?"
"'I' do not utilize the communications function referred to as 'name'. On Earth, any of my projections is referred to as 'wisp'."
"If the manifestation '$9' must use a 'name' to remain functional, it may use 'wisp'."
"Correct."
"A subset of the more general superset of bipedal organic units. A primitive example of the more complete evolutionary point of which 'I' am an example."
"That is correct. We are on Earth."
"Xorinia acts as a conduit for information between different continua, planes, dimensions. Xorinia also retains information which will improve Xorinia."
"The manifestation in proximity of '$9' is at location 'here-now' to observe energy @anomalies."
"The geographical superset commonly referred to by its local bipedal manifestations as 'valley' and 'Eodon' and 'here' is a source of energy stress."
"A @power source of significant relative magnitude exerts considerable distorting influence on this space-time region."
"Analysis of the situation indicates that at some temporal point in the 'past' an energy source bearing the Britannian vocal referent 'moonstone' embedded itself in this proximity."
"@Modification of the energies of said 'moonstone' have resulted in the geographical superset 'here-now' 'Eodon' 'Valley' being placed outside the normal space-time continuum."

"Life-units which in other 'here-now' positions have ceased to manifest on both individual and collective bases have adapted to the distortion by continuing to exist in both individual and collective senses."
"Continuing stress on the space-time continuum by the damaged 'moonstone' has resulted in scattering of small but volatile @distortions all through the space-time continuum."
"Stresses from power source called 'moonstone' exert tremendous influence on the space-time continuum. This results in ripples and holes in the continuum."
"This can create temporary points of intersection between space-time points -- that is, 'places' -- which should customarily enjoy no contact."
"Left uncorrected, this situation can permanently distort and blend space-time regions, perhaps @destroying them."
"Object containing the distorting energy is similar to objects which are called 'moonstones' in the dimension 'Britannia.'"
"This one has been subtly altered, and differs from other examples of its type in ways your language has no words for."
"Vocal interpretations of its physical state of being result in the words 'black' and 'stone'."
"Amounts of power indicated that the referent 'large' or 'enormous' should also be appended."
"Available data indicate that life-forms studying the power source 'moonstone' enacted energies upon it, modifying it beyond its original scope."
"These modifications have resulted in distortions to the space-time continuum."
"Unchecked emission of energies from power-source 'moonstone' can result in blending, blurring, and ultimately destruction of large regions of the @multiverse."
"'Multiverse' is a word-referent of your life-form; it signifies all reality in all universes."
"Where is a 'you' word-referent interrogative requesting data on space-time coordinates, correct?"
"It is impossible to relate space-time coordinates as this manifestation grasps them to coordinates as the life-form 'you' understands them."
"It is redundant for 'you' to make notification of 'your' intent to move to different spatial points."
"A short trip forward on the time continuum reveals that intent much more precisely. However, in the manner of 'your' life-form: 'Good-bye.'"

"The information 'I' have just given 'you' can be considered a free sample. If 'you' offer 'me' valuable information at a point further along the time continuum, 'I' will present 'you' with information of true value."
"The communications form 'you' refer to as 'language' is too inexact and interpretive. This manifestation cannot answer 'your' interrogative."
